The **Clinical Process** in acute surgical care encompasses the critical, time-sensitive workflows that occur from a patient's arrival at the hospital to the delivery of essential medical and diagnostic interventions. In [[danmark|Danmark]], these processes are rigorously monitored to ensure high standards of care, optimize patient outcomes, and identify areas for systemic improvement. The [[akut-kirurgi-databasen|Akut Kirurgi Databasen]] serves as the central national repository for tracking these clinical metrics, providing a comprehensive overview of how efficiently hospitals manage acute surgical patients.

A primary focus of the acute clinical process is the timely administration of medication. Under [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]], the database tracks the duration between hospital arrival and the administration of antibiotics. Nationally, the median time from arrival to receiving antibiotics is 4.6 hours [^src1]. This metric is vital for understanding systemic delays in treating infections or preparing patients for urgent surgical procedures.

Diagnostic imaging is another crucial component of the acute clinical workflow. Rapid assessment via computed tomography is often necessary to determine the correct surgical or medical pathway for acute patients. The national median time from hospital arrival to CT-scanning is 101 minutes [^src2]. Together, these metrics illustrate the operational realities of acute care in Denmark, highlighting the logistical and clinical workflows hospitals navigate to deliver timely interventions.
